To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The pQCD predictions of the pion and kaon form factors with the leading and next-to leading twist contributions are not precise.
the Sudakov corrections are important for the pion form factors at large Q2, and that

(a) The pion form factor is not well predicted in pQCD, (b) The twist-3 contribution is very large, (c) The twist-4 contribution is small, (d) The Sudakov corrections provide only a weak suppression of nonperturbative effects at experimental energy scales.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the pion electromagnetic form-factor within the perturbative QCD (pQCD) approach in the framework of a phenomenological model.
the phenomenological analysis of Sudakov effects and the twist-3 contributions in the pion electromagnetic form factors.
the phenomenological aspects of the Sudakov effects in hard exclusive processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pQCD predictions for the pion form factors are not precise enough to be compared with the experimental data at the present time.
the pQCD prediction for the pion form-factor is not precise.
the pQCD predictions for the pion form-factor at the experimental accessible region are in agreement with data within errors, however, with large uncertainties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the perturbative corrections in the pion electromagnetic form-factor can be large and the nonperturbatve corrections cannot be neglected.
Sudakov effects provide only a weak correction to the pion form factors, but the next-to-leading twist correction is large and should be included.
we have shown the Sudakov effect is important in the pion and kaon form factors, but not in a precise way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pion form factors are not precise.
the pion form factors are very sensitive to higher twist contributions.
Sudakov effects are not a panacea to the problems in the pQCT approach.
